nodes.description: HER performance comparison vs bare Pt(111) in 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Although there are fewer Pt sites available on the bare Pt(111) substrate in the presence of Ni(OH)2 clusters, the Ni(OH)2/Pt(111) electrode is ~7 times more active for the HER than the corresponding bare Pt(111) electrode in 0.1M KOH

nodes.description: Structure-dependent HER activity comparison on Pt(hkl) surfaces in alkaline solution
nodes.source_text: while only a small difference in activity between Pt low-index single crystal surfaces has been found in acid environments, a substantial difference in activity is found in alkaline solutions... the degree of activity, increasing in the order (110)>(100)>(111), is proportional to the density of surface defects

nodes.description: HER overpotential comparison at 50 A/m² across metal groups in 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: A bar graph of activities for HER represented as overpotential to achieve constant current of 50 A/m²... The green bars represent activities for Ni(OH)2 modified surfaces in 0.1 M KOH... the Ni(OH)2/M surfaces are, without exception, more active (~3-5 fold) than on corresponding bare substrates

nodes.characterization_summary: As-prepared Pt(111) electrode reveals flat terrace covered by few steps and Pt ad-islands with monatomic height.
nodes.evidence_snippet: an STM image of the as-prepared Pt(111) electrode reveals that the surface is composed of a flat terrace which is covered by few steps and Pt ad-islands with monatomic height (Figure 2b)

nodes.characterization_summary: As-prepared Pt(100) electrode shows ad-islands with square shapes and monoatomic height due to 'lifting' of (100)-hex phase forming (100)-(1x1) surface with well-ordered defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ad-islands with square shapes and monoatomic height are clearly evident on the as-prepared Pt(100) electrode (Figure 2c). The presence of such islands on Pt(100) is due to 'lifting' of a (100)-hex phase

nodes.characterization_summary: As-prepared Pt(110) surface shows irregular morphology even on 100×100 nm scale.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the case of the Pt(110) the STM image (Figure 2d) reveals that even on a 100×100 nm scale, the surface is far from ideal

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-islands/Pt(111) shows electrochemically deposited Pt ad-atoms resolved as two-dimensional features with diameters ∼1 to 3 nm and height of 1 atomic layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the STM image of Fig. 2e and 2f, the Pt ad-atoms can be clearly resolved as two-dimensional (2D) features with diameters of ∼1 to 3 nm and a height of 1 atomic layer (Fig. 2c)

nodes.characterization_summary: 3d-TM(OH)₂ clusters (Ni, Co, Fe, Mn) on Pt(111) are randomly distributed across terraces, grown as 3D islands by Volmer-Weber mechanism with spheroid-like shapes 7-10 nm diameter, ∼0.49-0.65 nm tall, constituting two layers of electrically conductive material; metal centers in 2+ oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: detailed examination of the nature and morphology of these 3d-TM hydroxides revealed that for all of them the metal center were in 2+ oxidation state... form randomly distributed clusters across the (111) terraces (STM images shown in Fig 3a–3e), grown as 3D islands by a Volmer-Weber mechanism, with spheroid likes shapes ranging from 7 to 10 nm in diameter and ~0.49-0.65 nm tall, constituting of two layers of electrically conductive material
